justification: Score is capped by check #2 of this review: one quote attributed to a named primary source does not exist anywhere on that source's page, and two more quotes are altered inside quotation marks. Everything else about the article is strong, but the brief's binding rule is 'never fabricate,' and the gauntlet's own list of what caps a score names fabricated or altered quotes explicitly, so this cannot be waved through as a nit. Details: (1) The Git Flow section attributes 'new small bugfixes ... other than that, no new features' to Driessen's original post as a direct quote. I fetched nvie.com/posts/a-successful-git-branching-model/ in full and ran a targeted full-text search for 'small', 'bugfixes'/'bug fixes' and 'no new features': none of the three appears anywhere on the page. The post's actual language for what a release branch may hold is 'last-minute minor bug fixes and preparing meta-data for a release,' and its actual prohibition, stated elsewhere, is 'Adding large new features here is strictly prohibited.' Neither sentence resembles the quoted text; this is not a paraphrase-with-drift, it is an invented sentence in quotation marks with a source link next to it. (2) The trunk-based development section quotes '"release branches are created on a just-in-time basis, are 'hardened' before a release ... and those branches are deleted some time after release."' The source (fetched in full) reads 'there may be release branches that are cut from the trunk on a just-in-time basis, are 'hardened' before a release (without that being a team activity), and those branches are deleted some time after release.' 'that are cut from the trunk' became 'are created' inside the quotation marks. (3) The same section quotes teams that '"employ feature flags in day to day development to allow for hedging on the order of releases"'; the source says 'use feature flags in day to day development to allow for hedging on the order of releases (and other good things ...),' not 'employ'. (4) In the Conventional Commits section, '"regardless of what type is used"' is attributed to the spec's SemVer mapping; two independent fetches of the live page both returned the actual wording as 'Commits with BREAKING CHANGE in the commits, regardless of type, should be translated to MAJOR releases' -- 'regardless of type,' not the phrase quoted. I could not re-run a web search to triple-check this last one (session search budget was exhausted), so I list it as minor/lower-confidence rather than major, but it fits the same pattern as the other three and should be re-verified against the live page before the next round. Every other quote I checked was accurate: the six-step GitHub Flow list, 'Your changes will not end up on the default branch until you merge your branch,' the branch-protection sentence, the draft-PR sentence, 'After you merge your pull request, delete your branch,' the Merge Commit and squash-merge descriptions from About pull request merges, the master/develop HEAD sentences, the --no-ff empty-commit defense, the hotfix-branches sentence, the full 2020 continued-delivery note, the 'deploy their major application to production with each commit' sentence, feat/fix MUST-use sentences, the '!' and BREAKING CHANGE footer rules, and the semver 0.y.z SHOULD-NOT-be-stable sentence and the git-tag release recommendation. So the problem is real but localized to four sentences, not systemic sloppiness -- which is exactly why it reads as fabrication risk rather than as a wholesale copy-and-garble problem: most of the article's dozens of quotes were handled carefully, and these four look like a reviser's memory of the source standing in for a re-check against it. Front matter and citations otherwise: all 9 listed sources are cited inline and all 9 inline external links match a listed source one-to-one (verified by extracting every markdown link target in the body and diffing against front matter) -- no orphaned citations and no missing ones, which is better bookkeeping than the pillar's first article managed. Originality is genuinely strong and would otherwise have scored well above 8.5: the article's organizing device (build one real branch history per model with a real teammate scenario -- storefront/discounts/cart-guard for trunk-based, landing-page/newsletter for GitHub Flow, ticketing/refunds/seats for Git Flow -- then read the difference straight off measured `git rev-list --count` numbers, 3 merges/7 commits vs 4 merges/11 commits) is not what 'git workflow' or 'trunk based development vs git flow' comparison pages do; the genre (Atlassian's comparing-workflows page among them) is diagrams and prose describing each model in the abstract, not executed sessions with real output and a working semver-bump script built and exercised across three repositories. The three diagrams, the four exercises (predict-then-check, squash-merge consequences, hotfix-reachability, model-vs-feature-count) and the closing decision table are original, not templated against sibling version-control articles, and the closing table earns its place instead of restating headings. Boundary with siblings is clean: the article explicitly defers merge mechanics, fast-forwards and --no-ff semantics to branching-and-merging.md and object/ref mechanics to how-git-works.md, cites their anchors instead of re-deriving them, and its own content (branch lifetime policy, release cadence, PR gating, commit-message convention, semver automation) does not overlap either sibling. No filler: first sentence states the two questions a branching model answers and moves straight into why the two models chosen differ most; no restated title, no 'in this article,' no summary-of-headings conclusion. No keyword stuffing: title, description and tags name the three real models by name rather than piling on query variants. No ad code. Toolchain disclosure ('Git 2.52 in Git Bash on Windows') appears once, mid-section, in the writer's own words, not as an opening provenance sentence. `node tools/run-code.mjs src/content/articles/version-control/git-workflows.md` passes: 'PASS version-control/git-workflows.md blocks=36 executed=18'. I did not run tools/verify-page.mjs (screenshots, Lighthouse, console/link check) -- that is outside this review's assigned steps and the design critic's job -- so consoleErrors and brokenLinks are left null rather than guessed; they are not part of why this score is capped.

issues.location: ## Git Flow section, paragraph beginning 'A release branch cuts from `develop`, bumps the version, and takes one last-minute confirmation the original post calls out by name:' -- the quoted phrase 'new small bugfixes ... other than that, no new features'
issues.problem: Fabricated quote. Attributed to Vincent Driessen's 'A successful Git branching model' as a direct quotation with a citation link right above it in the same section, but this sentence does not appear anywhere on that page -- confirmed by fetching the full page and searching it for every distinctive word in the quote ('small', 'bugfixes', 'bug fixes', 'no new features'), all with zero matches. The source's actual, real content on this point is split across two different sentences: 'last-minute minor bug fixes and preparing meta-data for a release' (what a release branch is for) and, separately, 'Adding large new features here is strictly prohibited' (what it is not for). Neither is what is quoted.
issues.fixLooksLike: Remove the fabricated quotation marks and either (a) paraphrase accurately and cite the real sentences, e.g. 'the original post allows only "last-minute minor bug fixes and preparing meta-data for a release" on it and states that "adding large new features here is strictly prohibited,"' with both fragments quoted verbatim from the live page, or (b) drop the direct-quote framing entirely and describe the rule in your own words with the existing citation link.

issues.location: ## Trunk-based development section, the sentence 'Once a change is worth shipping, trunk-based development leaves the timing to a separate step:' followed by the quoted clause 'release branches are created on a just-in-time basis, are '"'"'hardened'"'"' before a release ... and those branches are deleted some time after release.'
issues.problem: Altered quote. The source (trunkbaseddevelopment.com, fetched in full) reads 'there may be release branches that are cut from the trunk on a just-in-time basis, are '"'"'hardened'"'"' before a release (without that being a team activity), and those branches are deleted some time after release.' The article's version silently replaces 'that are cut from the trunk' with 'are created' inside the quotation marks -- a real wording change presented as a verbatim quote.
issues.fixLooksLike: Quote the actual sentence: '...release branches that are cut from the trunk on a just-in-time basis, are "hardened" before a release ... and those branches are deleted some time after release.'
